'''Mukul Sinha''' (10 February 1951 – 12 May 2014) was an Indian human rights activist and a lawyer at the [[Gujarat High Court]] in [[Ahemdabad]]. He was an active trade union leader and a trained physicist. He legally represented the families of the individuals who were killed in [[Gujarat]] following the [[2002 Gujarat riots|2002 riots]] and in [[Manipur]], in which he secured convictions of the politicians and police officers involved.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/gujarat-fake-encounters-are-similar-mukul-sinha/story-IxKf9JPn4Obk1bYYDmJ9tL.html|title=Gujarat fake encounters are similar: Mukul Sinha|last=Langa|first=Mahesh|date=8 July 2013|work=Hindustan Times|access-date=2017-07-11|language=en|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060303/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/gujarat-fake-encounters-are-similar-mukul-sinha/story-IxKf9JPn4Obk1bYYDmJ9tL.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mainstreamweekly.net/article5003.html|title=Remembering Advocate Mukul Sinha|last=Alam|first=Mahtab|date=21 June 2014|website=Mainstream Weekly|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140625150511/http://www.mainstreamweekly.net/article5003.html|archive-date=2014-06-25|url-status=dead|access-date=2017-07-11}}</ref> Along with his wife [[Nirjhari Sinha]], he founded and served as the president of Jan Sangharsh Manch (''trans.'' People's Struggle Forum), an independent civil rights organization with the aim of addressing issues of labour and workers rights. He was also a vocal critic of erstwhile Gujarat Chief Minister [[Narendra Modi]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.frontline.in/other/obituary/on-the-side-of-victims/article6048929.ece|title=On the side of victims|last=Katakam|first=Anupama|date=13 June 2014|work=Frontline|access-date=2017-07-11|language=en|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060310/https://frontline.thehindu.com/other/obituary/on-the-side-of-victims/article6048929.ece|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theweek.co.uk/world-news/58040/indian-election-narendra-modi-course-victory|title=India election: what kind of PM will Narendra Modi be?|date=16 May 2016|work=[[The Week]]|access-date=20 October 2016|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060305/https://www.theweek.co.uk/world-news/58040/indian-election-narendra-modi-course-victory|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ScrollObit" />

==Early life and education==
Mukul Sinha was born in [[Kolkata]] on 10 February 1951.<ref name="ScrollObit">{{cite news |last1=Janmohamed |first1=Zahir |title=Mukul Sinha, self-effacing Modi opponent and labour organiser who disliked being called a leader |url=https://scroll.in/article/664314/mukul-sinha-self-effacing-modi-opponent-and-labour-organiser-who-disliked-being-called-a-leader |access-date=28 July 2019 |work=Scroll |date=13 May 2014 |archive-date=9 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060331/https://scroll.in/article/664314/mukul-sinha-self-effacing-modi-opponent-and-labour-organiser-who-disliked-being-called-a-leader |url-status=live }}</ref> After completing his undergraduate studies in [[Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh]],<ref name="ScrollObit" /> he studied at [[IIT Kanpur]] where he received a master's degree in physics.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/noted-activist-and-lawyer-mukul-sinha-dies-561481|title=Noted Activist and Lawyer Mukul Sinha Dies|date=13 May 2014|work=[[NDTV|New Delhi Television Limited]]|access-date=20 October 2016|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060305/https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/noted-activist-and-lawyer-mukul-sinha-dies-561481|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Career==
Sinha joined the [[Physical Research Laboratory]] (PRL) in Ahmedabad in 1973 for doctoral research.

He became involved with social activism after the expulsion of workers at PRL in 1978. He organized the workers to fight for their rights, founding the Federation of Employees of Autonomous Research and Development, Education and Technical Institutes (FEARDETI),<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/india/india-others/mukul-sinha-who-fought-for-2002-riot-victims-succumbs-to-cancer/|title=Mukul Sinha, who fought for 2002 riot victims, succumbs to cancer|date=2014-05-13|work=The Indian Express|access-date=2017-11-29|language=en-US|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060306/https://indianexpress.com/article/india/india-others/mukul-sinha-who-fought-for-2002-riot-victims-succumbs-to-cancer/|url-status=live}}</ref> although this cost him his job in 1979.

===Jan Sangharsh Manch===
Subsequently, Sinha obtained a degree in law in 1988 and joined the Gujarat High Court as an advocate in 1989. He co-founded Jan Sangharsh Manch in 1990 under the aegis of the [[New Socialist Movement]] and organized a group of lawyers and individuals from different professions to work ''pro-bono'' on various issues of the general public ranging from trade-unions, housing, environment, natural calamities, and civil rights.<ref>{{cite web|title=At a Memorial, Hundreds Pay Tribute to a Gujarat Human Rights Champion|url=http://india.blogs.nytimes.com/2014/05/15/at-a-memorial-hundreds-pay-tribute-to-a-gujarat-human-rights-champion/|last=Janmohamed|first=Zahir|date=15 May 2014|website=New York Times|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150912064742/http://india.blogs.nytimes.com/2014/05/15/at-a-memorial-hundreds-pay-tribute-to-a-gujarat-human-rights-champion/|archive-date=12 September 2015|access-date=10 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.telegraphindia.com/1160807/jsp/nation/story_101073.jsp#.WAknqMlfsbs|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160807172130/http://www.telegraphindia.com/1160807/jsp/nation/story_101073.jsp#.WAknqMlfsbs|url-status=dead|archive-date=7 August 2016|title=Young 'hero' behind new Dalit movement|date=7 August 2016|work=[[The Telegraph (Calcutta)|The Telegraph]]|access-date=20 October 2016}}</ref> The group represented the [[2002 Gujarat violence]] victims and legally fought the Gujarat state government,<ref name="The Economic Times - 8 September 2013 - Narendra Modi still in PM race despite Vanzara letter bomb">{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/narendra-modi-still-in-pm-race-despite-vanzara-letter-bomb/articleshow/22398659.cms|title=Narendra Modi still in PM race despite Vanzara letter bomb|last=Dutta|first=Vishal|date=8 September 2013|work=[[The Economic Times]]|publisher=[[The Times Group]]|accessdate=28 September 2013}}</ref> in the [[Nanavati-Mehta Commission|Shah-Nanavati inquiry]].<ref name="The Hindu - 2 July 2011 - Destruction of records: Jan Sangharsh Manch planning to move court">{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/destruction-of-records-jan-sangharsh-manch-planning-to-move-court/article2152328.ece|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131214133438/http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/destruction-of-records-jan-sangharsh-manch-planning-to-move-court/article2152328.ece|url-status=live|archive-date=14 December 2013|title=Destruction of records: Jan Sangharsh Manch planning to move court|last=Dasgupta|first=Manas|date=2 July 2011|work=[[The Hindu]]|publisher=[[The Hindu Group]]|url-access=subscription|accessdate=28 September 2013}}</ref> The organisation has also fought for justice to the families of the victims in the fake encounter cases and exposed claims of the police and Modi's government branding them as terrorists to the public. The legal interventions by the organisation led the Supreme Court in the Sohrabuddin Sheikh case to pass the investigation from the Gujarat police to the Central Bureau of Investigation. This set a precedent as all the other cases taken up by JSM were handed over to the CBI and the investigation in all these cases established them as extrajudicial killings.<ref name="mukul tehelka">{{cite web|last=Tehelka bureau|title=The Only Thing The Minorities Once Got Were Bullets. Now We Are Getting Some Faith Back|url=http://www.tehelka.com/the-only-thing-the-minorities-once-got-were-bullets-now-we-are-getting-some-faith-back/|publisher=Tehelka.com|accessdate=28 September 2013|date=10 March 2013|archive-date=14 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131214000007/http://www.tehelka.com/the-only-thing-the-minorities-once-got-were-bullets-now-we-are-getting-some-faith-back/|url-status=dead}}</ref> His recommendations made after the [[2001 Bhuj earthquake]], titled "Kutch Quake Profile",<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/2001/20010506/nation.htm |title=IMD admits error in calculating quake epicentre |date=5 May 2009 |work=[[The Express Tribune]] |access-date=20 October 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090205222340/http://tribuneindia.com/2001/20010506/nation.htm |archive-date=5 February 2009 }}</ref> resulted in an injunction from the court to incorporate earthquake-resistant structures in the state of Gujarat.

===2002 Gujarat riots===
{{main|2002 Gujarat riots}}
Gujarat experienced large scale [[2002 Gujarat riots|communal violence and riots in 2002]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Burman|first=J. J. Roy|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0rpzmcHn-0kC&q=Gujarat+Unknown:+Hindu-Muslim+Syncretism+and+Humanistic+Forays|title=Gujarat Unknown: Hindu-Muslim Syncretism and Humanistic Forays|date=2005|publisher=Mittal Publications|isbn=9788183240529|page=186|language=en|access-date=16 September 2020|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060306/https://books.google.com/books?id=0rpzmcHn-0kC&printsec=frontcover&dq=Gujarat+Unknown%3A+Hindu-Muslim+Syncretism+and+Humanistic+Forays|url-status=live}}</ref> With [[Jan Sangharsh Manch]], he participated in the [[Nanavati-Mehta Commission]] appointed by the Government of Gujarat to seek justice for the victims.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.milligazette.com/news/10405-irreparable-loss-noted-lawyer-and-activist-mukul-sinha-passes-away|title=Irreparable loss, Noted lawyer and activist Mukul Sinha passes away|work=Milli Gazette|publisher=13 May 2014|access-date=20 October 2016|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060310/https://www.milligazette.com/news/10405-irreparable-loss-noted-lawyer-and-activist-mukul-sinha-passes-away/|url-status=live}}</ref> As a party to the lawsuit, he managed to obtain mobile phone 'call data records' (CDR) submitted by [[Indian Police Service]] officer [[Rahul Sharma (Gujarat police)|Rahul Sharma]]. A thorough analysis of these records enabled lawyers, activists and victims to cite the CDRs as evidence, implicating a number of political leaders and police officers. The CDRs of [[Maya Kodnani]] and [[Babu Bajrangi]] were crucial evidence in corroborating the testimonies of [[Naroda Patiya massacre]] victims. Finally, the special court convicted them for their role in the riots.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gujarat riots: How IPS officer Rahul Sharma exposed rioters|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/west/story/gujarat-riots-modi-government-rahul-sharma-139188-2011-08-11|last=Bhattacharya|first=D P|date=12 August 2011|website=India Today|access-date=10 May 2020|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060320/https://www.indiatoday.in/india/west/story/gujarat-riots-modi-government-rahul-sharma-139188-2011-08-12|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Electoral politics===
Mukul Sinha contested elections for the [[Gujarat Legislative Assembly]] in 2007 as a candidate from his own political party, the [[New Socialist Movement]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.outlookindia.com/national/the-man-who-keeps-knocking-news-286836|title=The Man Who Keeps Knocking|date=22 July 2013|work=[[Outlook (Indian magazine)|Outlook]]|access-date=20 October 2016|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060321/https://magazine.outlookindia.com/story/the-man-who-keeps-knocking/286836|url-status=live}}</ref> and in 2012 as an independent candidate. He contested the 2007 elections from [[Shahpur, Gujarat|Shahpur]], a constituency where Muslims formed the majority of the population, and the 2012 elections from [[Sabarmati]] in [[Ahmedabad]]. He lost both elections, securing only a few votes.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://ceo.gujarat.gov.in/download/AE2007/AC2007_070.pdf|title=Final Election Result, Shahpur constituency|access-date=21 October 2016|archive-date=22 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161022023418/https://ceo.gujarat.gov.in/download/AE2007/AC2007_070.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://ceo.gujarat.gov.in/download/Form20_2012/AC055.PDF|title=Final Election Result, Sabarmati constituency|access-date=21 October 2016|archive-date=22 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161022023208/https://ceo.gujarat.gov.in/download/Form20_2012/AC055.PDF|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Death and legacy==
Sinha died of [[lung cancer]] on 12 May 2014.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last=Kumar|first=Devesh|date=13 May 2014|title=Noted Activist and Lawyer Mukul Sinha Dies|work=NDTV|url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/noted-activist-and-lawyer-mukul-sinha-dies-561481|access-date=10 May 2020|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060305/https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/noted-activist-and-lawyer-mukul-sinha-dies-561481|url-status=live}}</ref> He is survived by his wife Nirjhari Sinha and their son [[Pratik Sinha]], who runs the [[fact-checking]] portal ''[[AltNews.in]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.livemint.com/Politics/b8AgLS4EO2P24wmuKxsq5M/Gujarat-riots-activist-Mukul-Sinha-dies-at-63.html|title=Gujarat riots activist Mukul Sinha dies at 63|date=13 May 2014|work=[[Mint (newspaper)|Mint]]|access-date=20 October 2016|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060341/https://www.livemint.com/Politics/b8AgLS4EO2P24wmuKxsq5M/Gujarat-riots-activist-Mukul-Sinha-dies-at-63.html|url-status=live}}</ref> According to his wishes, his body was donated to [[Ahmedabad Civil Hospital]] for cancer research.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lawyer, social activist Mukul Sinha passes away|url=http://www.tehelka.com/2014/05/lawyer-social-activist-mukul-sinha-passes-away/|date=12 May 2014|website=Telheka.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161021005509/http://www.tehelka.com/2014/05/lawyer-social-activist-mukul-sinha-passes-away/|archive-date=21 October 2016|access-date=10 May 2020}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

Journalist [[Rana Ayyub]] wrote an obituary for Sinha, remembering her personal loss and his legacy.<ref>{{Cite web|title=My Baba, the revolutionary - Mukul Sinha|url=https://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-my-baba-the-revolutionary-mukul-sinha-1988388|last=Ayyub|first=Rana|date=2014-05-14|website=DNA India|language=en|access-date=2020-05-10|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060341/https://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-my-baba-the-revolutionary-mukul-sinha-1988388|url-status=live}}</ref> He was posthumously awarded the second Bhagirath Human Rights Award (BHRA) by the Bhagirath Memorial Fund Committee set up at the Centre for Social Studies (CSS), [[Veer Narmad South Gujarat University]], [[Surat]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Mehta|first=Yagnesh Bharat|date=15 February 2017|title=Late Mukul Sinha to get Bhagirath Human Rights Award|work=Times of India|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/surat/late-mukul-sinha-to-get-bhagirath-human-rights-award/articleshow/57153997.cms|access-date=10 May 2020|archive-date=9 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060340/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/surat/late-mukul-sinha-to-get-bhagirath-human-rights-award/articleshow/57153997.cms|url-status=live}}</ref> Activist [[Jignesh Mevani]] worked under Sinha's mentorship before becoming [[Member of the Legislative Assembly (India)|MLA]] from [[Vadgam]], Gujarat.<ref>{{cite news|last=Raza|first=Danish|date=20 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210209060341/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/in-depth-jignesh-mevani-s-journey-from-a-dalit-activist-to-vadgam-mla/story-T9N0QvSF6jVaah8tjKPlQI.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Dabhi|first=Parimal A|date=26 December 2017|title=Ex-journalist, lawyer, aspiring politician: Meet Jignesh Mevani, face of the Gujarat Dalit agitation|work=Indian
